text: I need a break. Somebody cover for me.
Okay. The swap is instant. Every planet stays put, moving at the same speed.
Hey! I'm Proxima, the closest star to you.
You're only an eighth of the Sun's mass. That's not enough to hold any of us.
Wait. Why am I drifting?
We're all drifting!
Every planet flies off into deep space. No orbit means no year and no seasons.
From the ground, you're just a dim red dot, and you keep shrinking.
Within a week, Earth drops below freezing. Within a year, it's about minus seventy.
The only warm spots left are near volcanoes and deep underground.
Sirius A. Two times the Sun's mass. Twenty-five times brighter.
Your stronger gravity bends my path into a long oval.
Every lap, I dive closer than Mercury is now. A full year takes about four and a half months.
At the close end, I get ten times more light than at the far end. Talk about brutal seasons.
From the ground, you're a blue-white sun nearly twice as wide as ours. The oceans boil away.
Huh. Out here, it finally feels warm.
Yep. Your icy moons could finally melt.
Hello... small one.
You're so huge, you reach past Mars. Mercury, Venus, Mars and I are all inside you.
You also weigh about eighteen Suns. Your pull drags even Neptune in.
Bro, I'm thirty times farther out than Earth!
Doesn't matter. Before you fall, you see a red sun twenty-five times wider than ours.
So, still want a replacement?
Nope. One was too light. One was too heavy and bright. One was way too big.
You are just right. Never leave again.
